steps.reasoning_content:
Wait, `urlparse('///i8n.example2.com/302')` actually returns an empty netloc and `/i8n.example2.com/302` as the path. This means `urljoin` would incorrectly append the path to the original domain, resulting in `http://www.example.com/i8n.example2.com/302` instead of the expected `http://i8n.example2.com/302`. The test is failing because the redirect logic is not handling this three-slash URL correctly.

This looks like a known Scrapy bug, possibly related to PR #3794, where the redirect middleware didn't correctly handle relative redirect locations starting with `///`. The fix likely involves using `request.urljoin` or adding specific logic for these cases in the redirect middleware.

The fix for the `///` redirect URL case involves prepending the scheme to the location if it starts with `//`. This correctly handles cases like `///i8n.example2.com/302` by turning it into `http://i8n.example2.com/302`, which `urljoin` can then process properly. The buggy version, however, fails because it passes the `///` URL directly to `urljoin`, leading to an incorrect concatenation with the original domain.
